item.title: Alleged plot to shift poll: it’s fake news, we’re unaware — Presidency
item.description: •ADC-PCC insists on allegation plot, warns Tinubu •Reps call for INEC briefing on preparedness By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Luminous Jannamike & Gift ChapiOdekina THE Presidency has described as fake news allegations that the Federal Government was planning to shift the January 16 elections. African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, had earlier raised an alarm over alleged plot to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, into shifting the January 16 presidential election, warning President Bola Tinubu against seeking to evade an electoral verdict. But Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, while reacting to the allegation, said the government was unaware of any move to shift the election. “The federal government is not planning to shift the date of the election or postpone any election. This is not in the works; the federal government is unaware of this, and this is just fake news as far as we are concerned.” However, the council said it had received information that INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, would be summoned to the Presidential Villa and instructed to alter the election timetable, with just 80 days to the poll. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the council urged Tinubu to abandon any such move and called on Amupitan to reject any instruction to change the date and immediately make any such approach public. “The election date belongs to Nigerians. It must not be rewritten behind closed doors at the Villa,” the council said. It said Nigerians had endured three and a half years of soaring prices, shrinking incomes and relentless hardship, insisting that they must be allowed to judge the Tinubu administration at the ballot box on January 16. “A government that has made life this difficult for Nigerians must not be allowed to postpone its day of judgment,” it said. While acknowledging Ebola as a serious public health concern, the council said health professionals must be allowed to contain the disease, adding that INEC must take necessary steps to protect voters and election workers. It cited the position of the Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, NCDC, that there was currently no reason to postpone the election, warning against using the health emergency as a political justification for delay. The council also put INEC, domestic observers and international election monitors on notice, demanding that any proposal to alter the timetable be made openly, backed by published health evidence and subjected to public scrutiny. “The Presidency must not use a health emergency to escape an electoral verdict,” it added. At press time, the electoral commission was yet to react to the development. item.title: FG approves East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW
item.description: •Pays N1.23trn of N3.3trn power sector debt By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA—THE Federal Government said yesterday it has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West super grids, as part of efforts to strengthen the national electricity network and raise transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu, at the Council Chamber, Presidential Villa, Abuja. He explained that the projects would improve grid resilience and enable the country evacuate more electricity to consumers. “The East and West Super Grids are not projects for one part of the country. They cut across the north and south of Nigeria, strengthening the backbone that must carry power from where it is generated to where it is needed,’’ he said. The initiative is designed to address one of the sector’s central contradictions: Nigeria has more than 13,000MW of available generation capacity, but its transmission network can reliably wheel only about 5,000MW. Tegbe said the super grids would improve resilience, reduce grid instability and allow more electricity to reach homes, businesses and industries. He said: “The target is simple. We want a grid that can evacuate the power we already have, not one that leaves generation stranded while consumers remain in darkness.’’ The minister explained that the corridors would strengthen transmission links from Sokoto through Abuja and other locations into parts of southern Nigeria. Beyond the super grids, the council approved three immediate interventions for Abuja and the Lagos axis, two of the country’s most important electricity demand centres. The first is a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line connected to the Katampe Transmission Substation, a major hub serving the North-Central region. The second covers the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical node supplying Lagos. The third will reconstruct and upgrade the 35.6-kilometre Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu 132kV single-circuit line into a double-circuit line to serve rising demand along the Lagos–Shagamu corridor. “These are not glamorous projects, but they are the projects that determine whether power actually gets to the consumer,” Tegbe said. On sector liquidity, the minister disclosed that the federal government had paid N1.23 trillion of the N3.3 trillion owed gas suppliers and other power-sector stakeholders. “We have paid N1.23 trillion, and we intend to finish the job. But we must also stop new debts from accumulating,’’ he said. The post FG approves East, West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Deputy Senate President faults Osinbajo over alleged comments on gloomy economy, democracy
item.description: *Says Tinubu addressing long-standing challenges By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, APC, Kano North, has taken a swipe at former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo over the gloomy picture he painted of Nigeria’s economy and democratic governance. Senator Barau Jibrin who noted that Osinbajo got it wrong , said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was taking steps to address what he described as longstanding challenges confronting the country. According to Jibrin, while Osinbajo’s concerns, particularly those drawn from Afrobarometer surveys on Nigeria and other African countries were valid, the government needed to improve communication with the people to highlight ongoing efforts to address the challenges. Recall that Osinbajo, who served as Vice-President under former President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023, had expressed concern in his lecture about the failure of democratic governance among citizens across Africa after almost three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries. Citing Afrobarometer surveys, Osinbajo, who was defeated by President Bola Tinubu during APC presidential primary, ahead of the 2023 elections, highlighted widespread dissatisfaction with democratic institutions, economic hardship, declining public confidence in government and diminishing youth participation in electoral politics. He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with the way democracy was working in their respective countries. Osinbajo also cited findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent said their economies had deteriorated. He further expressed concern over the rising cost of living, unemployment, inadequate access to healthcare and declining voter turnout, warning that persistent hardship could weaken public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people. But replying the former vice president at a public lecture, titled ‘’Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,’’ in Yola, Adamawa State, to commemorate the 59th birthday of Governor Ahmadu Fintiri yesterday, Barau described Osinbajo’s lecture as thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating. He,however, said the gloomy picture painted by the surveys was being addressed and that the gaps were partly attributable to inadequate communication between governments and citizens. He said: “I know he is a very good orator, a good public speaker and an intellectual to the core. Having said that, I am compelled to make some comments on the paper. item.title: Manufacturers raise alarm over N1.35trn alternative power costs, 18,935 job losses
item.description: *Say growth crawls at 1.41%, despite broader economic recovery *Urge FG to cut energy, financing costs lAcknowledge govt’s import-duty, value-added tax relief on 875 pharmaceutical raw materials By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Omotola Aremo LAGOS — Manufacturers under the aegis of Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Employers Federation, CANMPEF, said yesterday they were facing mounting pressure from soaring energy costs, expensive credit, weak consumer demand and job losses, despite improvements in the country’s key macro-economic indicators in 2025. The federation also raised alarm over the worsening cost of doing business, citing an estimated N1.35 trillion spent by local manufacturers on alternative power in 2025, alongside the loss of 18,935 manufacturing jobs in the first half of the year. President of CANMPEF and Vice President of the Dangote Group, Chief Devakumar Edwin, who raised the alarm at the Federation’s 46th Annual General Meeting, AGM, in Lagos, called on the Federal Government to urgently address the high cost of energy and financing, harmonise taxes and levies and strengthen support for local production. He said: “Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.87 per cent in 2025, up from 3.38 per cent in 2024, while headline inflation declined and the foreign exchange market became more stable. However, these improvements have yet to translate into meaningful gains for manufacturers. “Manufacturing grew by only 1.41 per cent in 2025, compared with 1.20 per cent in 2024, while its contribution to real Gross Domestic Product fell to 8.05 per cent from 8.24 per cent.’’ Edwin described the situation as a major concern for the industrial sector, stressing that macro-economic stability must translate into stronger industrial output, job creation and export growth. “Our central message is that this stability must now translate into competitiveness in the form of sustainable jobs, increased output and exports. ‘’Although the economic reforms introduced from mid-2023 had delivered measurable improvements in inflation, foreign exchange stability and economic growth, manufacturers continue to grapple with high operating costs that undermined production and investment. Most of these gains have yet to reach the factory floor,” the CANMPEF president stated. ‘Electricity supply is major constraint’ He identified electricity supply as one of the most significant constraints confronting manufacturers, particularly producers of chemicals, plastics, rubber, glass, ceramics and other non-metallic mineral products, many of which depended on energy-intensive production processes. “Despite installed grid capacity exceeding 13,000 megawatts, average delivered generation remained below 5,000MW, against estimated demand of about 18,345MW. The shortfall, attributed to gas-supply constraints, transmission bottlenecks and recurring grid collapses, has forced many manufacturers to depend on alternative power sources at considerable expense,’’ Edwin said. item.title: Pushback over N70,000 allowance
item.description: By Idowu Isamotu, Daniel Adaji, Abuja & Abdullateef Aliyu, Lagos The leadership of the Trade Union Congress (TUC) on Wednesday rejected the federal government’s proposed six-month N70,000 transportation allowance for workers. The Congress, which described the government’s plan as a “haphazard measure” to cushion the effects of fuel subsidy removal, demanded an immediate salary increment for workers. Daily Trust reports that the government had on Tuesday approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants, beginning in November, to cushion the impact of rising living costs. The approval was one of the resolutions reached at a conciliation meeting between the federal government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday. This followed renewed pressure from organised labour over workers’ welfare, the rising cost of living and outstanding agreements. At the meeting, the government also approved the payment of outstanding peculiar allowance arrears, effective from May 1, 2026, in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. The meeting, which lasted several hours, witnessed a lot of disagreements and a series of back-and-forth, according to a senior labour leader who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity on Wednesday. “What we first demanded during the meeting was immediate reduction of the fuel price, but those on the government side opposed it. This led to disagreements for hours before the chief conciliator appealed to everyone. “After all the back-and-forth, the government side proposed N70,000 transport allowance for six months, not tagged wage award this time, and we reached a consensus on this,” the source said. Although the parties agreed to immediately constitute a Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee, they failed to agree on the effective date for implementing the national minimum wage. A memorandum of understanding signed at the end of the meeting, where the resolutions were contained, showed that leadership of the TUC was not part of the decision. Checks showed that the MoU was signed by the Director-General of Budget, Timi Yakubu; NLC President, Joe Ajaero; the Permanent Secretary, Service Welfare Office, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Dr Garba Abdul S.U. and the Minister of Labour and Employment, Maigari Dingyadi. TUC kicks The TUC argued that while it is good to negotiate minimum wage, which will affect other cadres of workers, the government must raise the wage level immediately. Speaking to journalists in Abuja shortly after rising from its National Administrative Council (NAC) meeting, the President of TUC, Festus Osifo, who was flanked by the General Secretary, Nuhu Toro, said there are no laws or historical practices stopping the government from doing so. He maintained that temporary wage awards are not sustainable, arguing that the wage award agreed on October 2, 2023 was to be implemented until a minimum wage was fixed in 2024 but was not enforced holistic

item.title: IGP faces contempt for estate leader’s arrest despite pending court order
item.description: By Innocent Anaba The leadership of the GTHomes Estate Residents Association in Lekki area, Lagos, has initiated contempt proceeding against the Inspector General of Police, IGP, before a Federal High Court sitting in Lagos, over the arrest of the outgoing legal adviser of the association, Mr. Austin Akpomreta, despite a subsisting order for parties to maintain status quo. Akpomreta was arrested by members of the police from the Police Monitoring Unit, Abuja on Wednesday last week and whisked to Abuja, despite a pending court order. The arrest came weeks after reports emerged that the IGP had cautioned police formations against the misuse of police processes in matters with clear civil underpinnings and against practices that could encourage forum shopping by complainants dissatisfied with outcomes at other police formations. Akpomreta, who is one of the applicants in a suit pending before the Federal High Court, Lagos, was reportedly picked up on Wednesday morning despite a subsisting court order directing all parties to maintain the status quo pending the determination of the application before the court. He was said to be on his way to an unrelated court hearing when accosted by operatives of the Police Monitoring Unit and transported to Abuja. The arrest is reportedly in respect of the same dispute that is the subject of ongoing fundamental rights proceedings before the court, following disagreements relating to estate administration and utility services. The suit was instituted following concerns over repeated attempts by a resident, to use various police formations across Lagos and Abuja in relation to a dispute that multiple police commands and formations had reportedly regarded as civil in nature but was being framed as criminal, to invoke police involvement. All respondents in the matter, including the IGP, the Police Service Commission, and the investigating police officer in the matter, are said to have been duly served with the originating court processes as well as the order of the court directing parties to maintain the status quo pending the hearing and determination of the application. Akpomreta wife, Faith, said her husband’s arrest while the court order remains in force, “raises serious questions about compliance with judicial processes. and respect for the authority of the court.” The applicants have consistently maintained that the issues in dispute are civil in nature and are properly suited for determination by a court of competent jurisdiction and are urging all institutions and parties connected with the matter to respect the authority of the Federal High Court and allow the judicial process to run its course without intimidation, harassment, or actions capable of rendering the court proceedings nugatory. item.title: AU accredits Nigeria’s counter-terrorism centre for West Africa
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The African Union (AU) has accredited Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), under the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), as a Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism for West Africa and the Sahel. The accreditation fulfils President Bola Tinubu’s vision, announced at the High-Level African Counter Terrorism Meeting held in Abuja in April 2024, to position the NCTC as a regional hub for intelligence sharing, operational coordination, specialised training and capacity building against terrorism and violent extremism. A statement issued on Thursday by Abu Michael, Head of Strategic Communication at the NCTC, said the designation marked a significant milestone in Nigeria’s contribution to collective African security. It said the recognition formally positioned the centre to support AU member states, particularly those in West Africa and the Sahel, through enhanced counter-terrorism cooperation and institutional capacity development. According to the statement, the accreditation gives the NCTC an expanded regional mandate to provide specialised training, joint threat analysis, research, technical assistance, exchanges of lessons learned and other forms of counter-terrorism support. The accreditation was announced on October 27, 2026, by the Acting Director of the African Union Counter Terrorism Centre (AUCTC), Dr Idriss Mounir Lallali, on behalf of the AU Commission’s Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security, at the conclusion of the African Lessons Learned Forum in Abuja. Lallali said the recognition followed a rigorous assessment of the NCTC’s institutional capacity, governance, training programmes, analytical capabilities, coordination mechanisms and adherence to human rights and the rule of law. He explained that the accreditation process began with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the AU and the NCTC in September 2025. This was followed by a technical assessment mission conducted by the AUCTC in Abuja in December 2025, which produced an accreditation roadmap outlining the institutional standards required for recognition. Since then, the NCTC has worked to strengthen its governance structures, develop training curricula and operational procedures, improve its analytical and coordination functions, and reinforce its commitment to human rights and the rule of law. The statement said the successful completion of the accreditation requirements reflected the centre’s institutional development and the collaborative efforts of ONSA, NCTC leadership and personnel, as well as strategic partners. Announcing the decision, Lallali said: “It is therefore my pleasure to announce that the African Union is accrediting the NCTC as an African Union Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism. “This decision will be conveyed formally to the Government of the Federal Republic of Nigeria through a Note Verbale. item.title: ALTON urges states to scrap telecoms right-of-way fees
item.description: Association says charges account for up to 60% of fibre deployment costs By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) has urged state governments to abolish right-of-way charges on telecommunications infrastructure, warning that the fees account for up to 60 per cent of fibre-optic deployment costs in some states and discourage network expansion into underserved communities. The association said scrapping the charges, particularly in rural areas and locations with limited commercial prospects, would lower infrastructure deployment costs, attract investment and help bridge Nigeria’s digital divide. ALTON Chairman, Engr. Gbenga Adebayo, made the call on Tuesday on the sidelines of a plenary session sponsored by IHS Nigeria at the 2026 Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja. Right-of-way charges are fees imposed for permission to access and use public or private land, roads and other designated spaces to install fibre-optic cables and related telecommunications infrastructure. Adebayo said the high cost of obtaining right-of-way approvals had become a major obstacle to fibre deployment, making it difficult for operators to justify investments in communities where anticipated revenue might not cover infrastructure costs. “Today, the cost of right-of-way amounts to a significant part of the cost of fibre deployment. For every one kilometre of fibre that you deploy, in some of the states, the cost of right-of-way can be as high as 50 to 60 per cent of the cost of deploying the entire infrastructure,” he said. He called for legislation to make right-of-way access for telecommunications infrastructure free, particularly in rural communities and other areas where expected commercial returns were unlikely to attract private investment. According to him, removing the charges would make network expansion more affordable and encourage operators to extend services to communities with poor or no connectivity. The ALTON chairman also urged the government to introduce incentives for telecommunications companies investing in areas where infrastructure deployment costs exceeded the revenue they could reasonably expect to generate. He said existing government intervention mechanisms, particularly the Universal Service Provision Fund (USPF), could be deployed more strategically to support network expansion in underserved locations. “There are also intervention funds. We have the Universal Service Provision Fund, which is designed for special intervention in those areas that are lacking coverage,” Adebayo said. He dismissed suggestions that telecommunications operators were unwilling to invest in rural communities, arguing that the challenge was largely economic and could be addressed through appropriate incentives and targeted government support. item.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea in League Cup shoot-out, Man City survive scare
item.description: Liverpool beat Chelsea in a dramatic penalty shoot-out to reach the League Cup quarter-finals, while holders Manchester City survived a scare against Brighton on Wednesday. In a clash between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso, it was the Liverpool manager who took the bragging rights in the last-16 tie at Anfield. A 1-1 draw in normal time set the stage for the shoot-out as Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers netted from the spot, only for Cody Gakpo to equalise with a penalty of his own just before half-time. Chelsea’s Valentin Barco hit the post in the shoot-out before Liverpool’s Kostas Tsimikas wasted a chance to win it when he blazed over. Ryan Gravenberch was denied by Chelsea keeper Mike Penders, but Giorgi Mamardashvili saved Emmanuel Emegha’s kick to keep Liverpool alive. After Joe Gomez scored for Liverpool, Blues defender Wesley Fofana miscued into the Kop as the hosts advanced. It was former Liverpool midfielder Alonso’s third defeat in his three visits to Anfield as a manager following losses with Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and Real Madrid in 2025. In their debut campaigns at Liverpool, Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot both reached the League Cup final and Iraola is on course to follow in their footsteps with the 10-time winners of the competition. Alonso made just four changes to the Chelsea side that lost 2-0 at home to Tottenham on Saturday, while Iraola made seven changes from Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday. Rogers put Chelsea in front with a 40th-minute penalty after Gravenberch clattered into Moises Caicedo. But Liverpool were level three minutes later with a penalty of their own as Gakpo converted from the spot following Fofana’s handball. At the Etihad Stadium, City were pushed to the brink by Brighton in a 2-2 draw before winning on penalties. City boss Enzo Maresca made nine changes after Saturday’s loss at Aston Villa — which ended the leaders’ 100 percent start to the Premier League campaign. – Rulli stars for City – Erling Haaland, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Gianluigi Donnarumma were among the City stars rested. Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter’s shot past Geronimo Rulli from five yards. Mateo Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards. Rutter restored Brighton’s lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam’s cut-back. Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki’s 72nd-minute free-kick to equalise for City. Kovacic’s penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shoot-out, but Rulli denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight. The sides meet again in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday. Bournemouth extended their blistering run with a 3-0 win against Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium. item.title: Ballon d’Or winner Kane watches as Bayern cruise into German Cup last 16
item.description: Newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was left on the bench as Bayern Munich sailed to a 6-1 win over second-tier Magdeburg in the German Cup last 32 on Wednesday. Bayern had no difficulty without their star striker, with Michael Olise grabbing a double and Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown and teenager David Santos Daiber also getting on the scoresheet. Kane received a guard of honour from his Bayern teammates before kick-off as the 75,000 fans at the Allianz Arena saluted the Ballon d’Or winner, two days after his triumph in London. Bayern got some more good news pre-match, with coach Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital, five days after collapsing at training on Friday. “We’re also winning for him of course,” Brown said of Kompany. “It’s really good that he’s back home now. He should get some rest, but hopefully we’ll see him again soon.” Olise tapped in an excellent Saibari assist from close range after 10 minutes but the unfancied visitors levelled five minutes later through Mateusz Zukowski. Olise returned the favour by setting up Saibari midway through the opening half and added a third from the spot early in the second half before smiling and pointing to Kane, Bayern’s regular penalty taker, on the bench. Teenage forward Lennart Karl set up goals for Davies and Brown before Santos Daiber added more gloss to the victory with a stoppage-time goal. Kane remained on the bench for the entire match, with Saturday’s home Bundesliga clash with Borussia Dortmund in mind. Bayer Leverkusen came from two goals down to win 5-2 against Nuremberg, with defender Edmond Tapsoba netting twice and Patrik Schick, Jonas Hofmann and Lucas Vazquez scoring goals. Earlier on Wednesday, Germany forward Deniz Undav’s 90th-minute strike took Stuttgart to a 1-0 win at 10-man Paderborn. Stuttgart, finalists in 2025, had a one-man advantage after Laurin Curda’s 37th-minute red card but could not break down a stubborn Paderborn. After striker Ermedin Demirovic had two efforts saved, Undav took matters into his own hands and turned in a Chris Fuehrich cross with extra time looming. “The win is what matters most,” Undav said. “I honestly don’t care whether I’m the one who scores, and that’s the truth. We won, we’re through to the next round — on we go.” Japan forward Keisuke Goto scored twice in the final 15 minutes to overturn a 2-1 deficit as Freiburg won 3-2 at home against Wolfsburg. Goto’s Japan teammate Kento Shiogai also bagged a brace, while Freiburg’s Igor Matanovic opened the scoring. Elsewhere, second-division sides Dynamo Dresden and Hertha Berlin both won 2-0 against Schalke and Jeddeloh respectively, while Kaiserslautern eliminated Hannover. item.title: Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to US
item.description: Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country’s rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro’s defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday. “I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming “electoral fraud.” “I will lead the opposition from here,” he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the “leader,” rather than “president.” Bolsonaro, 45, touched down earlier Wednesday in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami. President Donald Trump’s hard-right administration has strong links to Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022. Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil’s election was “very strange” but told reporters he “won’t get involved” in Flavio Bolsonaro’s claim to the presidency. Details of how Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to US soil are still emerging. He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering. With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador. A police source told AFP that Bolsonaro’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, but the senator has also held Italian nationality since 2023, according to Italian documents seen by AFP. The US Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared “with applicable immigration laws and procedures.” The travel ban was issued by powerful Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led the case against Flavio Bolsonaro’s father and is a controversial figure hated by the Brazilian right. Flavio Bolsonaro had vowed to seek the justice’s impeachment if he were elected — which up until Lula’s comeback in the runoff had looked increasingly likely. – ‘Shameful’ act – Lula, who won the election with 51.8 percent of Sunday’s vote, called Flavio Bolsonaro’s departure a “shameful” act. “A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide,” he said in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration on Tuesday. But Brazil police issued a statement Wednesday saying that he was not considered a fugitive. There was controversy in neighboring Argentina, where opposition lawmakers demanded to know how Bolsonaro had managed to transit through the country. item.title: Solid Minerals: FG Inaugurates Nigeria-US Committee On Strategic Cooperation
item.description: The Federal Government has inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja to advance the partnership with the US. This came weeks after the Federal Government and the United States of America signed a memorandum of understanding to boost the development of Nigeria’s solid minerals sector. The agreement was signed on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly between Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau, at the Nigerian Mission House in New York, United States. The minister, who inaugurated the committee, however, refuted claims that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to America. “I inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja to advance our partnership with the United States and set the record straight on reports claiming Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to America,” Alake stated in a post on X. “Let me be very clear. Nigeria has not sold its mineral assets.” He explained that the agreement signed with the US was a government-to-government framework designed to connect American investors with Nigerian businesses. “It is about attracting investment, sharing technology, expanding local processing and creating jobs. “Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s leadership, we are determined to move beyond an economy heavily dependent on oil,” he said. The minister stated that Nigeria’s mineral resources must create greater value at home and deliver lasting benefits to Nigerians. “That is why local processing is now a key requirement for investors seeking mineral titles. “Our partnership with the US offers an opportunity to match Nigeria’s vast resources with the capital and technology needed to build a stronger mining industry. The progress we are seeing in mineral processing reflects this direction,” he added. Alake urged the committee to approach the responsibility with diligence, identify viable investment opportunities and turn the agreement into measurable results that support President Tinubu’s $1 trillion economy target. According to him, the focus is ensuring that Nigeria’s mineral wealth creates jobs, strengthens our economy and delivers real value to our people. At the signing of the MoU in September , the minister had said that the implementation would achieve the economic diversification goals of the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu and boost industrial growth. Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau, at the Nigerian Mission House in New York, United States, during the pact signing. The Deputy Secretary of State Landau was quoted as expressing strong agreement with Nigeria’s position, adding that as Africa’s fastest-growing economy and most populous country, Nigeria is a regional power that deserves partnership with the US.

item.title: No ministers paid billions for appointments, APC insists
item.description: By Dickson Omobola The All Progressives Congress, APC, Wednesday, denied claims that ministers pay billions of Naira to secure appointments, saying comments made by its Presidential Campaign Council spokesperson, Alwan Hassan, referred to historical practices rather than the current administration. Hassan had alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently seek to recover the money. Speaking during an interview on Arise TV, Hassan said: “The way Asiwaju is hands-on on the expenditure of our revenue is fantastic and I love it. A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money.” Reacting to the statement, which has generated backlash, National Publicity Secretary of APC, Felix Morka, questioned how ministers who allegedly paid billions to secure appointments would recover such sums within Nigeria’s budgetary framework. Speaking on Primetime, an Arise TV programme, Morka said Hassan had explained that his remarks were not directed at the current administration but were made in a historical context. His words: “What he was referring to was not really about this administration, but he was speaking in historical context. What he said left a lot of ambiguity, some have suggested that he was speaking about appointments. He was clear as well when he said that what he was describing predated APC. As a citizen listening to him, I thought he was simply conflating systems. When he came back and said it predated the APC, that suggested to me that his frame of thought was really located, not in the present, but really in the past. “When you are a public commentator, sometimes you generalise without really specifically drawing those lines of distinction between moments. If I say there’s corruption in Nigeria, I’m not necessarily saying that this government is corrupt. am not here to sort of overanalyse or justify comments. I think that, in due time, he alone will have to come tell what he had in his mind. But from talking to him, what I understood, after the fact, was that he was simply speaking historically, to say that ministers generally in our country have had this really terrible record of engaging in that behaviour. “If ministers are paying billions to get appointed, how exactly, within what we know to be Nigeria’s budgetary frame, do you recoup the billions you paid to get appointed? I don’t think that is really something that, personally, I am willing to even imagine. He made a comment in historical context, as he explained it. In other democracies, lobbying for appointments is not something unusual. In the United States, there are firms that are contracted to lobby for individuals to get appointed to office. Those are usual things that happen in the background.prior to appointments. “I think the concern here is that when lobbying becomes monetised, where people pay money to operators or to individuals with influence

item.title: 2027: Kwankwaso warns INEC over alleged AI-generated images in voter register
item.description: ‎ ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has warned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that alleged irregularities in the preliminary voter register could undermine the credibility of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso raised the concern in a statement posted on his official Facebook page, following reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other questionable records in the register. ‎ ‎He warned that failure to properly investigate the allegations could weaken public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral system ahead of the elections. ‎ ‎According to him, the development raises serious questions about the integrity of the voter registration process and the measures put in place by INEC to prevent electoral manipulation. ‎ ‎”With the 2027 elections approaching, INEC must provide Nigerians with clear and convincing answers,” he said. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso questioned how the suspicious photographs found their way into the register, whether the individuals involved were genuinely registered and if their identities were properly verified. ‎ ‎While welcoming INEC’s decision to investigate the allegations, the former governor insisted that Nigerians deserved more than assurances from the electoral body. ‎ ‎He called for a thorough, transparent and independent investigation, saying the findings must be made public and anyone found responsible held accountable under the law. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso also demanded a comprehensive independent audit of the preliminary voter register to identify questionable entries, duplicate registrations and possible artificial identities. ‎ ‎He, however, stressed that the exercise must not deny eligible Nigerians their constitutional right to vote. ‎ ‎”Our democracy cannot afford any compromise in the integrity of the voter register. Every eligible Nigerian must have the right to vote, and every vote must count,” he said. ‎ ‎The former governor further warned against the use of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, to manipulate the electoral process. ‎ ‎”Nobody should be allowed to exploit technology, including artificial intelligence, to undermine our electoral system,” he added. ‎ ‎Kwankwaso maintained that the credibility of the 2027 general elections would depend largely on the accuracy and integrity of the voter register. ‎ ‎”The credibility of the 2027 elections begins with a credible voter register, and INEC must get its act together,” he declared The post 2027: Kwankwaso warns INEC over alleged AI-generated images in voter register appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Chelsea Win As Bayern, Madrid Share Points In Women’s Champions League
item.description: Goals from Ellie Carpenter and Kadeisha Buchanan were enough to secure a second win for Chelsea in this season’s Women’s Champions League on Wednesday, while Bayern Munich came from two goals down to draw with Real Madrid. Chelsea, who reached the final in 2020-21, opened their campaign with a win and a draw despite scoring just once in their first two games. They looked nailed on for another win in the first half at Plough Lane as they dominated the game without getting a goal. Alyssa Thompson hit the crossbar while Aggie Beever-Jones, put away by a superb pass from Hannah Hampton, was denied by a last-ditch challenge from Shukurat Oladipo. That changed in the 51st minute when Wieke Kaptein cut the ball back for substitute Carpenter, making her 50th Champions League appearance, who slid the ball under the goalkeeper Rachele Baldi. Melvine Malard missed a golden chance to put the game to bed, but Buchanan sealed it a minute from time, heading Kaptein’s cross into the Roma net. Bayern Munich’s Spanish forward Edna Imade (R) celebrates scoring the 1-2 goal with her teammates during the UEFA Women’s Champions League – League phase, Matchday 3 – football match between FC Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in Unterhaching near Munich, southern Germany, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) There was a moment’s silence before kick-off at the Sportpark Unterhaching in Munich as a mark of respect after at least 68 people were killed in a train crash near Madrid earlier on Wednesday. Real Madrid, who were all wearing black armbands, took an early lead when Athenea found the net in the seventh minute. They doubled their lead 15 minutes later when former Bayern forward Lineth Beerensteyn headed home from close range, her first goal for Madrid in the Champions League since her move in the summer. Real Madrid’s Spanish forward Athenea del Castillo (C) celebrates scoring the opening goal with her teammates during the UEFA Women’s Champions League – League phase, Matchday 3 – football match between FC Bayern Munich and Real Madrid in Unterhaching near Munich, southern Germany, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) / ALTERNATIVE CROP Bayern hit back shortly after when Edna Imade met Klara Buhl’s corner from the left and powered her header into the net. And they drew level in the 52nd minute when Momoko Tanikawa curled in from the edge of the box after Madrid keeper Merle Frohms parried out a shot from Linda Dallmann. Swiss side Servette dispatched Belgium’s OH Leuven 5-1 with Paola Hernandez and Gloria Marinelli scoring two goals each. Wednesday’s late matches see Arsenal host Benfica while eight-time winners Lyon are at home to Inter Milan. AFP The post Chelsea Win As Bayern, Madrid Share Points In Women’s Champions League appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Atiku challenges Tinubu to prove he’s in Makkah
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide daily proof of his presence in Makkah for Umrah, alleging that the planned pilgrimage could be a smokescreen for a trip to France. Atiku said Nigerians deserved to know the President’s actual destination, daily engagements and the purpose of the trip, raising questions about a reported $20 billion loan request involving a French business partner. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said intelligence available to him suggested that Tinubu might make only a brief appearance in Makkah before proceeding to France. He called on the Presidency to release clear, current and date-stamped photographs and videos each day showing Tinubu at the Kaaba and performing the rites of Umrah. “Nigerians deserve verifiable proof of the President’s presence in Makkah and a transparent account of his daily activities in the Holy Land,” he said. Atiku also questioned whether the trip was connected to the President’s health and the reported $20 billion loan request, urging the Presidency to address the concerns and disclose the full itinerary. The former vice president said he and other Nigerians would join Tinubu in prayers for the country’s peace and progress, but warned against invoking religion without sincerity. “No one should invoke the name of Almighty Allah in vain,” he said, insisting that a spiritual mission undertaken on behalf of the nation must be treated with seriousness and transparency. He maintained that Nigerians were entitled to know how the trip was being funded and demanded verifiable evidence of the President’s whereabouts and activities. item.title: Natural resources not enough for national prosperity – Makinde
item.description: Gov. Seyi Makinde said natural resources alone cannot guarantee a prosperous national economy. Makinde stated this on Wednesday at the 10th anniversary celebration and inauguration of the CapitalSage Holdings Global Headquarters in Ibadan According to the governor, sustainable growth depends on entrepreneurship, skills, knowledge and intensive production. He noted that while Nigeria is richly endowed with natural resources, sustainable economic prosperity depends on entrepreneurs’ willingness to take risks, innovate, and invest. He stressed that states and nations that had achieved real prosperity did so by moving beyond resource abundance to building human capital and productive enterprises that create jobs and value. He noted that Oyo State’s economic transformation agenda was anchored on supporting entrepreneurs and private sector-led industrialisation as a pathway to shared prosperity. The governor assured investors of his administration’s continued support through enhanced security, investment facilitation, and other measures aimed at promoting business expansion and economic growth. He urged stakeholders to recognise the critical role of private businesses in creating economic opportunities, generating employment, and strengthening local industries. Makinde, who described the inauguration as a celebration of entrepreneurship, congratulated the company on building a thriving business conglomerate, comprising about 20 companies. He added that having the conglomerate’s headquarters in Ibadan would further reinforce the city’s position as a leading business hub and investment destination. He also expressed the state’s confidence in competing favourably with Lagos in attracting investments and hosting major business operations. He assured investors that his administration remained committed to supporting businesses to grow and expand, describing a thriving private sector as key to the state’s economic future. (NAN) The post Natural resources not enough for national prosperity – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen kill 36-year-old man, injure pastor in fresh Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Gunmen have killed a 36-year-old man, injured a pastor and left another person missing in an attack on Lamor community in Pushit District of Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State. A member of the community, Nehemiah Bulus, who confirmed the incident to journalists in Jos on Wednesday night, said the attack occurred at the farm of Pastor Apollos Charly in Lamor. “Mr Steven Bala, aged 36, was killed, Pastor Apollos Charly was injured, and Mr Danbaba Libet, aged 57, is missing,” Bulus said. “Reports reaching us indicate that gunmen that have been terrorising communities in Plateau State attacked the victims at Pastor Apollos Charly’s farm,” he said. Bulus said the incident occurred in “Lamor, Pushit District, Mangu Local Government Area, Plateau State.” He condemned the attack, describing the killing of an innocent person and the injury to a pastor as unacceptable, and called on security operatives to intensify efforts to protect residents and prevent further bloodshed. “We condemn this senseless attack in the strongest terms. No community should be subjected to this kind of violence, and innocent people should not continue to lose their lives,” Bulus said. “We appeal to the relevant security agencies to investigate the incident, track down those responsible and bring them to justice. “ “We also urge security operatives to strengthen their presence in the area to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety,” he added. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful. The post Gunmen kill 36-year-old man, injure pastor in fresh Plateau attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: No reason to fear INEC will postpone elections – SDP
item.description: By Henry Umoru The national leadership of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, has said that there are no reasons to fear that the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will postpone the 2027 general elections. Speaking with Vanguard on Wednesday on allegations that INEC was planning to shift the January 16 election, the SDP National Publicity Secretary, Araba Rufus Aiyenigba, said, “For the SDP, there is no justifiable reason to entertain fears that the Commission could be tempted to postpone the scheduled 2027 general elections. “The public health scare associated with the Ebola reports has been dismissed by the Nigerian Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), and claims of Ebola being weaponised has been strongly rejected by the health authorities. “We are yet to have a credible reason to doubt the readiness of INEC for the general polls. The Commission has not given us any reason to be so concerned because there is no sign that surfaced. “The challenges of security crisis, which could form the basis for election postponement possibility, are yet to be in a dimension of grave concerns. “It is also necessary to note that the worries that have been variously expressed by the lack of implementation of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, particularly delay in the display of voters’ register has been addressed by the Commission with the online upload of the preliminary voters register on its portal. “While the SDP remains vigilant and will keep its eyes on the ball, the party remains optimistic and positive-minded that nothing will impede the successful conduct of the 2027 general elections. “It is the nation’s best interests for the elections to hold and be seen to be fair and credibly conducted.” The post 2027: No reason to fear INEC will postpone elections – SDP appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Inter leave it late again in Serie A as Bologna sink AC Milan
item.description: Inter Milan returned to the Serie A summit with a nervy 2-0 win at bottom side Venezia on Wednesday, while a Samuel Mbangula hat-trick sealed a 4-2 win for Bologna at San Siro to inflict a first league defeat of the season on AC Milan. Champions Inter drew level with Lazio on 25 points at the top ahead of a hotly anticipated Milan derby meeting with their rivals on Saturday. Ruben Amorim’s side will go into that game on the back of losing their unbeaten streak after Alphadjo Cisse’s double was not enough to avoid a defeat that left the Rossoneri fifth on 18 points. Fresh off a pulsating stoppage-time turnaround against Fiorentina on Sunday that marked their fifth comeback win of the season, Inter thought they would have to fight back from behind once again when Lion Lauberbach fired the rock-bottom hosts in front after 29 minutes. The champions were handed a reprieve when it was ruled out for offside, but had goalkeeper Ivan Provedel to thank for keeping the scores level at the break as he diverted a Lauberbach effort off the bar. Venezia have picked up just three points all season but looked the likelier to make the breakthrough as Gianluca Busio fired over unmarked from 12 yards before Akor Adams rounded Provedel to score, only for the offside flag to save Inter again. Last season’s Serie B champions stunned Napoli with a win on new coach Davide Nicola’s debut and another shock result looked possible until they were undone in painful fashion late on. Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal diverted dangerous deliveries into their own net in the space of two minutes to ensure Inter returned to the top of the standings and Venezia remained rooted to the bottom. – Mbangula magic downs Milan – At San Siro, a lengthy injury list featuring the likes of Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Mario Gila restricted Amorim’s options for the first midweek round of the season, while the Milan coach left Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric on the bench. Mbangula, making his full debut for Bologna, swept home the opener inside eight minutes, but the visitors were soon pegged back when an Arthur Theate error gifted Cisse a simple finish. The Milan teenager struck again in the 27th minute, volleying home a Fikayo Tomori cross, but the game was turned on its head once again in the space of two second-half minutes to stun the San Siro crowd. The unfortunate Davide Bartesaghi turned a free-kick into his own net before Mbangula struck again with a composed control and finish in the box just after the hour mark. The 22-year-old then completed a memorable night four minutes from time when he beat Mike Maignan for a third time with a smart finish after Bologna robbed the ball in midfield. Bologna sealed back-to-back wins for the first time this season to move into 11th place on 11 points. Elsewhere, Adrian Bernabe had a penalty saved by Maduka Okoye as struggling Parma and Udinese played out a 0-0 draw. Later on Wednesday, Juventus and Napoli travel to Genoa and Monza respectively

item.title: Tinubu To Present 2027 Budget Before End Of 2026
item.description: President Bola Tinubu is expected to present the 2027 Appropriation Bill to the National Assembly before the end of 2026. The Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite, disclosed this on Wednesday when she briefed State House Correspondents on some of the outcomes of the Federal Executive Council Meeting chaired by President Bola Tinubu at the Council Chamber of the State House. She also said that the FEC had officially endorsed the National Development Plan 2026–2030 alongside new legal frameworks designed to tackle child stunting and boost national food security. Speaking with correspondents following the council meeting, Uzoka-Anite announced the key approvals while reflecting on the successful conclusion of the 32nd edition of the Nigerian Economic Summit (NES) held in Abuja from October 26 to October 28. Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite. She said FEC also approved a Revised National Policy on Food and Nutrition (2026) to replace older frameworks to establish sustainable financing and strengthen inter-ministerial collaboration across agriculture, livestock, health, education, and development partners. Earlier, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, clarified that the $21.7 billion borrowing proposal transmitted to the National Assembly by President Bola Tinubu is an investment in assets and not for spending. Oyedele explained that the proposed $21.7 billion plan represented a multi-year investment plan spanning roughly five years rather than an immediate drawdown. He disclosed that $10.6 billion of the money was slated for critical transport links, including the Sokoto–Badagry Highway, Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, and the Kano–Kaduna Metro Rail. Oyedele said that over $7.9 billion of the loan would be sourced from multilateral and bilateral development partners (led by $5 billion from the World Bank) at an average interest rate of just ~2.1 per cent. He said $3.3 billion is earmarked directly for state government projects, with an additional $1.45 billion set aside for the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), ​out of the overall package. item.title: Full list: Ballon d’Or of All Time as Ronaldo emerges winner
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning campaign has been voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The Ballon d’Or announced Ronaldo as the winner of its “Ballon d’Or of All Time” (BOAT) vote on Wednesday, after fans had their say in a poll that opened on October 1 and closed at 23:59 Paris time on October 27. The vote asked fans to choose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season. The result was shared on Wednesday by football transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano via his X page. Lionel Messi’s 2012 season finished second, with Ronaldo’s 2017 campaign third. Messi’s 2023 season took fourth, while Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign rounded out the top five. The top ten also includes Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 seasons, plus Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns. Ronaldo’s winning season came in 2007–08 with Manchester United, where he scored 42 goals in all competitions, including 31 in the Premier League and seven in the Champions League. United won both the Premier League and Champions League, with Ronaldo scoring in the final against Chelsea. His league tally earned him the European Golden Shoe, and he went on to win his first Ballon d’Or later that year. The Portuguese legend subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five. item.title: TUC To FG: You Don’t Need Minimum Wage Negotiations To Increase Salaries
item.description: The Trade Union Congress (TUC) has told the Federal Government that it does not need to negotiate a new minimum wage before increasing workers’ salaries, insisting that a permanent pay rise would provide more lasting relief than the proposed ₦70,000 transport allowance. ﻿ Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, TUC President Festus Osifo said salary increases and minimum wage negotiations were two separate issues that could be addressed independently. “On the 8th of October, we had a National Administrative Council meeting of the TUC; we reached an agreement, and we addressed a world press conference, and in that agreement our position was very clear: you don’t need to negotiate minimum wage before government could intervene in the plight of workers, not at all,” Osifo said. He argued that governments could increase workers’ salaries without waiting for a new minimum wage agreement, noting that minimum wage negotiations were not the only means of improving workers’ welfare. “There are some countries in the world where the minimum wage may not be negotiated for 25 years. The minimum wage can be fixed for 25 years, but at every point in time, there is always an intervention from government. The unions in that country engage the government for increment in salary,” he said. Osifo added that the distinction between minimum wage and salary increases gave the government room to improve workers’ earnings without reopening minimum wage negotiations. “Increment in salary and minimum wage are very different. Minimum wage is minimum, but there is no maximum wage, so what that means is that the government, on its own, can look at how to improve the plight of the workers by increasing the salaries of workers. This is done in all establishments, so you don’t need a minimum wage conversation for government to increase salaries,” he said. The TUC president spoke on the sidelines of the Federal Government announcing a ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026. The approval followed a conciliation meeting with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Tuesday, October 27, to address issues raised by organised labour. However, the TUC rejected the proposed allowance, calling instead for an increase in workers’ salaries and the implementation of the agreement with the Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU). Explaining the rejection, Osifo said the congress wanted a more sustainable and permanent intervention rather than a temporary measure. “If what you are offering today is a temporary measure, we reject it; we want something that is much more sustaining and something that is more much more permanent,” he said. item.title: Niger State Assembly Commends Army For Foiling Attack By Bandits
item.description: ‎ ‎The Niger State House of Assembly has commended troops of the Nigerian Army for repelling a major attack by bandits on communities in Rafi Local Government Area of the state, which left one soldier dead and three others injured. ‎ ‎The House also called for the establishment of additional military bases in vulnerable communities to strengthen security, prevent bandits from regrouping, and improve rapid response to distress calls. ‎ ‎The commendation followed a motion moved by the member representing Rafi Constituency, Zubairu Zanna, during plenary on Tuesday. ‎ ‎The lawmaker praised the troops for their courage, professionalism and gallantry in confronting the armed men, saying their intervention prevented what could have resulted in a massacre of innocent residents. Niger State is in North-Central Nigeria ‎ About two weeks ago, more than 100 suspected bandits reportedly invaded communities along the Zungeru-Tegina Road but were met with stiff resistance from the Army, which successfully repelled the attack. ‎ ‎Although one soldier reportedly died from gunshot injuries while three others sustained injuries, several bandits were neutralised during the encounter, and motorcycles were recovered. ‎ ‎Zanna urged the Nigerian Army and other security agencies to sustain their operations and strengthen their presence in the affected communities to prevent further attacks. ‎ ‎He stressed the strategic and economic importance of the communities, noting that the establishment of a Forward Operating Base (FOB) would help prevent criminal groups from regrouping and launching fresh attacks. ‎ ‎According to him, the absence of military bases and strategically positioned security formations along identified vulnerable corridors could limit the ability of security personnel to respond swiftly to distress calls. ‎ ‎The lawmaker further observed that difficult terrain, extensive forests and inadequately secured rural routes in parts of the state, particularly Rafi Local Government Area, provided opportunities for criminal groups to infiltrate communities, establish camps and hideouts, and launch attacks on innocent residents. ‎ ‎He therefore called on the Niger State Government to urgently engage the Federal Government on the need to establish additional military bases and strengthen security deployments in vulnerable communities, particularly along routes frequently used by bandits. ‎ ‎The Speaker of the House, Abdulmalik Sarkindaji, who presided over the plenary, called for a minute of silence in honour of the fallen soldier and offered prayers for the speedy recovery of those receiving medical treatment.
